title: 10th Sitting of third session of 2026
summary: The Majlis held the preliminary debate on a government bill amending the Tax Administration Act (3/2010), which would require taxpayers to pay 50% of a disputed MIRA assessment, and 100% in some cases such as related-party transactions, before appealing to the Tax Appeal Tribunal. Government-aligned members said it closes loopholes used by large businesses, while opposition members questioned changing the threshold again after it was set at 25% earlier this year and asked what tax revenue is spent on. The House then debated and passed a General Affairs Committee report amending Majlis rule 191, which opposition members said limits debate on resolutions; an amendment to remove the added clause failed. The tax bill was accepted 54-11 and sent to the Economic Committee. Part of one speech is garbled in the source text.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill, saying large businesses avoided tax through appeals and waivers while small businesses were penalised.
Criticised past MDP governments' debt and unfinished projects; the chair asked him to return to the bill.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Raised council salaries, medicine shortages, hospital staff pay and mental health helpline demand; the chair asked him to stay on the bill.
Said the Majlis can no longer debate resolutions freely.
Moved an amendment to remove the clause (n) added to rule 191(sh).

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said frequent tax-law changes erode trust and a larger deposit will not speed up tribunal cases; linked the bill to government revenue needs.
Objected to the Speaker's remarks in the debate and to how members must address the chair.
Asked whether President Muizzu had served as a minister under an MDP government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill, saying some large businesses delayed tax payments through appeals and election-time waivers.
Presented the General Affairs Committee report on the rule 191 amendment as committee rapporteur.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Opposed new tax measures before the budget, asked what tax revenue funds, and questioned requiring 100% upfront payment given long appeals.
Seconded the amendment to remove clause (n) from rule 191.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill, saying the earlier 25% included fines, so the new rules may benefit businesses.
Said the rule 191 change is minor and resolutions can still be debated after a floor vote.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked what tax revenue is spent on and questioned payments linked to the Ras Male project and the dollar rate.
Said the rule 191 change restricts the Majlis's oversight role and reflects outside business influence.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the government bill requiring part or all of a disputed tax assessment to be paid before appeal, to close loopholes and transfer-pricing abuse by large firms.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill but said tax appeals can take 13-15 years and urged faster resolution and more resources for the Tax Appeal Tribunal.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Questioned raising the upfront payment from 25%, set this year, to 50%, saying frequent changes harm investor and public trust.
Said requiring 100% before appeal effectively removes the right to appeal; asked for review at committee stage.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill as an administrative fix to loopholes that let large firms withhold hundreds of millions through tribunal appeals.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Fully supported the bill and described government reforms on debt repayment and clearing the fisheries payment backlog.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, saying the 2010 tax system strained small businesses; listed government projects in Dhidhdhoo and invited Hussain Ziyad to visit.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the rule 191 change continues a series of limits on Majlis debate; cited pending resolutions on teacher and health-worker pay and atoll electricity bills.
